subject: Custom SLA addendum and order form language for Harmonia Health
messages:
From: Procurement Team <procurement@harmonia.com>
To: stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: Legal Team <legal@harmonia.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 08:16:00 -0700
Subject: Request: custom SLA addendum & order form language

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for taking this. Procurement and Legal at Harmonia are aligning on an enterprise MSA + order form for a dedicated Redwood deployment, and we need a tailored SLA addendum (availability + latency commitments) to attach to the SOW. Attached is a short outline of our desired commitments and constraints (Harmonia_SLA_Request.pdf). Key asks: 

- Availability: 99.95% monthly across multi-region (primary us-east-1, failover us-west-2)
- Latency: p95 generation latency <= 150ms for typical conversational traffic; need a p99 tail target and clarity on measurement window
- Exceptions: carveouts for scheduled maintenance, third-party cloud provider outages, and planned model upgrades that may require short cache-warm periods
- Order form language: we need a short exhibit to include in the order form that references the MSA and the availability exhibit, and a clear credit schedule for outages exceeding the SLOs

Timeline: procurement intends to complete legal review and procure by May 1. Can you provide: 1) a draft availability exhibit ready for our counsel to redline, 2) a short list of measurable evidence (telemetry/metrics) that Redwood will provide, and 3) recommended order form wording (one paragraph) for dedicated capacity?

We can set up a 30-minute redline session if helpful — ideally next week.

Thanks,
Sandra Lee
Senior Procurement Manager
Harmonia Health
Attachments: Harmonia_SLA_Request.pdf
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Procurement Team <procurement@harmonia.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: custom SLA addendum & order form language

Hi Sandra —

Appreciate the clear asks and timeline. I took a pass at the practical path forward and attached a draft availability exhibit (redwood_availability-exhibit-draft.docx) to get the conversation started. High level:

- We can support a 99.95% monthly availability commitment across two-region failover, with specific exceptions and an evidence matrix.
- For latency, we recommend committing p95 at 150ms for the stated traffic profile and providing p99 as an operational target (we typically couple p99 with a higher credit/exception schedule because tail behavior is sensitive to burst patterns).
- Order form language: I included a short paragraph that links the exhibit to the order form and references the credit schedule.

Next steps I propose:
1) Please confirm the expected request volume profile (avg requests/sec and expected burst size) and the primary regions you expect Redwood to serve.
2) Priyom, can your team prepare the legal-friendly order form paragraph and flag any MSA cross-references we should include?
3) David, can you add an evidence/runbook deliverable that shows what telemetry we will provide for escalations and credits?

If that sounds good, I can schedule a 30-min redline session for Tue/Thu next week.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Sales Manager, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_availability-exhibit-draft.docx

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: custom SLA addendum & order form language

Thanks Stephanie — looping in a quick technical summary and evidence bundle. Attached is a short runbook and telemetry package (evidence-runbook.zip) that maps metrics we can provide for credit adjudication and incident reviews. Highlights: 

- Measurement windows: we measure availability on a per-region monthly window; failover is defined as route-level failover between configured endpoints.
- Latency SLOs: p95 <= 150ms (achievable for conversational workloads with our default batching and caching), p99 we recommend a softer commitment — we can set an operational p99 target of 450ms with an escalation path (credits at tighter thresholds).
- Canary/rollout: because this is a dedicated capacity deployment, we strongly recommend a 30-day canary period before activating the strict SLA credit schedule to account for cache warm and model tuning.

We should call out third-party provider outages (e.g., regional AZ failures) as an exception and include a short clause on notice and evidence submission procedures. Priyom — tagging you to review proposed order form phrasing in the attached draft and advise on MSA cross-ref language.

David Kim
Director, Reliability Engineering
Redwood Inference
Attachments: evidence-runbook.zip

Cc: Legal Team <legal@harmonia.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: custom SLA addendum & order form language

Stephanie —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the draft materials. We reviewed the exhibit and the runbook internally. A few notes from our counsel and ops: 

- Harmonia is comfortable with a 30-day canary prior to full SLA enforcement.
- For latency, counsel would like p95 at 150ms in the exhibit and a clearer definition for how p99 is measured (rolling 30-day window vs monthly aggregation). Can you reflect the rolling 30-day approach in the exhibit?
- We propose one small change to the credit schedule around sustained partial degradation (we will bring a suggested wording to the redline session).

Next: we will circulate an internal redline of the exhibit by Thu EOD and set a 45-minute session for Friday to walk through comments. I've attached our signature matrix and internal timeline (Harmonia_signature_matrix.xlsx) and included a DocuSign placeholder for later (https://docusign.com/placeholder/HARM-SLA-3429). Our HubSpot record for the opportunity is: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/company/HC-3429.

Look forward to the redline session.

Best,
Sandra Lee

Harmonia Health
